subject: Defining signals and ownership: Senior ↔ Staff calibration for Serving role
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Calibration: Senior ↔ Staff signals for Serving (candidate Alyssa Chen)

Hi team,

We have Alyssa Chen on the schedule for next week (Greenhouse GH-30921). Before interviews start I want to align on the concrete signals we expect for Senior vs Staff candidates for the Serving role — especially around ownership granularity, impact scope, and operational troubleshooting. I attached the candidate pack and a draft of interview anchors (interview-anchors-v2.md).

Proposed focus per interviewer (please confirm or propose changes):
- System design (Markus): emphasis on architecture tradeoffs for high-throughput low-latency LLM serving and rollout strategies.
- Reliability & on-call (Naomi): incident triage + postmortem reasoning; look for debugging methodology and blameless escalation.
- Ownership & product judgment (Grace): prioritization with limited infra budget; tradeoff framing.
- Implementation deep-dive (Marissa / panel): code-level reasoning, performance hotspots, and quantization/optimization fluency.

Two specific ask areas where I want clear anchors:
1) What concrete example distinguishes a Senior owning a service (multiple sprints) vs a Staff leading cross-team migrations (multi-quarter, sets roadmap)?
2) What is a pass/fail signal on operational maturity during an on-call scenario? (e.g., runbook authoring, RCA framing, hypothesis-driven debug).

Logistics: earliest slot confirmation pending — Marissa, can you lock calendars?

Thanks,
Evelyn

--

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Calibration: Senior ↔ Staff signals for Serving (candidate Alyssa Chen)

Evelyn — thanks for the clear framing. A couple quick points from the bar-raiser lens:

On the Senior vs Staff split:
- Senior: owns a service end-to-end, can independently design and deliver features that change latency/cost characteristics within a team boundary. Look for ownership of 1–2+ major rollouts and clear metrics improvement (latency, p50/p95, cost/token).
- Staff: drives cross-team changes (kernel or routing changes) that require coordination with infra, ops, and product; sets standards or abstraction layers used by multiple teams. Evidence: led design for a multi-team rollout OR authored a migration plan that reduced unit cost across product.

Operational maturity signal: runbook + hypothesis-driven debug + playbook contribution. For on-call scenario, a Senior should be able to triage to a root cause candidate and apply a mitigation; a Staff should identify systemic remediation (e.g., KV cache redesign) and a roadmap to prevent recurrence.

I recommend adding a short live debugging mini-exercise for the technical screen (15 min) — give a degraded-serving trace and ask the candidate for the top 3 hypotheses and a mitigation plan. That separates mere familiarity from practical operational skill.

(Quoted for context)
> On Tue, 20 Apr 2027 at 09:12, Evelyn Hart wrote:
> We have Alyssa Chen on the schedule for next week ... Two specific ask areas where I want clear anchors...

I'll take system design and the mini-debug exercise if the panel agrees.

Thanks,
Markus

1) Interview scope confirmed: Markus (system design + debug mini-exercise), Naomi (on-call/incident triage), Grace (ownership/product tradeoffs), Marissa will coordinate panel and implementation deep-dive slots.

   - Staff: multi-team migrations or abstractions with cross-team adoption and roadmap influence; authorship of mitigation roadmap.
3) Panel action: annotate interview-anchors-v2.md with 2 example evidence items by Thursday EOD.
4) Logistics: Marissa to finalize invites; Sarah/GaleTech to confirm candidate availability for the two windows.

I'll capture these decisions in the debrief template (link in the Drive folder) and ask the panel to use the rubric during scoring. If anyone wants to swap interviewer ownership, flag now.

Thanks — looking forward to the panel,
